# Art readiness after the f18 replay import

This read-only review inspected Git source at f18a50d904c57ae1652f157b946ebd39d8d8923c, product source at 453c2218af9973b9eca8fb78392435bd9d46a740, the installed Phaser source, and the retained failure files. It did not execute product code, tests, builds, imports or browsers, rehash large payloads, or modify repository files.

The saved failure establishes incomplete artwork, not its underlying cause. `browser/browser-native-acceptance.json` in `/tmp/ovf-native-combat-f18a50d-retry-20261001-zssa25k5` records replay mode, tick zero, paused, art enabled, loaded false, 100 manifest assets, 32 resident atlas pages, 366.5933837890625 MiB decoded and five rendered units. The stderr stack fails in `native-context.mjs:96` at replay-import readiness, before the endpoint seek. The preceding charge-stop-moving replay completed at tick 38. Its initial envelope equals the interrupted replay's initial envelope as parsed JSON. The later hold command occurs at tick 41, so it has not run in the displayed replay state.

## Concrete source mechanisms

Product paths below are under `/home/morgana/.codex/worktrees/final-combat-proof/orcs-vs-Fairies`, read from the pinned Git tree. ArtRuntime.ts, GameScene.ts and main.ts have no Git diff between product453 and proof f18.

`src/game/ArtRuntime.ts:26` assigns the manifest and queues the required atlas pages and environment images in the manifest file-complete callback. `ready()` at lines35-41 checks frame-name uniqueness, required assets, custom textures, environment textures and every required animation frame. `loaded` at line43 exposes its stored boolean. `src/game/GameScene.ts:149` calls ready once during create; there is no later call or retry. A false result remains false throughout the 60-second harness wait.

Five rendered units do not prove complete art. `ArtRuntime.ts:79` and lines92-94 count successful entity draws independently of complete. `loadedAtlasPages` at line44 counts every resident manifest atlas, and does not identify which required pages are missing. The pinned manifest has 23 fairy pages and 23 orc pages. The replay roster is fairies/orcs with no content bundle, and built-in definitions require those ordinary unit/building IDs (`src/core/content.ts`, `src/core/content-registry.ts:114`, and `ArtRuntime.ts:23`). If the browser used that pinned manifest, 32 resident pages means at least14 of the expected46 are absent. The actual manifest response was not captured, so the condition must remain stated.

Phaser can start create after image failure without a page exception. `node_modules/phaser/src/loader/filetypes/ImageFile.js:108` decodes an XHR response via an Image object; its onerror at line125 calls onProcessError. `node_modules/phaser/src/loader/File.js:479` writes a console error and marks the file errored. `node_modules/phaser/src/loader/MultiFile.js:249` marks the atlas failed and writes a console error. `node_modules/phaser/src/loader/LoaderPlugin.js:1126` describes completion after files have loaded or errored; loadComplete at line1137 emits COMPLETE after exhausting the queues. This supplies a concrete path to a manifest plus some textures, a running scene, and a latched false art flag. Network failure, invalid response bytes and image decoding failure remain possible; none is identified by the saved report.

Replay import and endpoint seeking have different art lifecycles. `src/main.ts:268` verifies the archive and forks at its initial tick. launch at lines201-225 retires the prior Phaser.Game and constructs a fresh GameScene/Game, triggering preload. Later endpoint seeking at line310 invokes the product's `GameScene.restart`, whose implementation at `GameScene.ts:262` resets sprites and game state without reloading textures or rerunning ArtRuntime.ready. The failure occurred before this reuse path.

## Diagnostic ownership and weaker hypotheses

`scripts/acceptance/native-context.mjs:14` deliberately omits camera and DOM readiness fields from snap. `src/main.ts:453` returns window.rts only when scene.cameras.main exists, so the successful failure snapshot supports a main camera existing at capture; it does not preserve its numeric values. Top-level report.display was captured by `verify-native-acceptance.mjs:82` after the initial menu match, before any groups ran. It is not the failure camera.

The green Replay loaded notice proves completion of the import callback rather than artwork readiness. `src/ui/SessionTools.ts:111` emits success after the action returns. `src/main.ts:272` launches asynchronously through retirement, and GameScene.create later calls onReady even if art is incomplete (`GameScene.ts:150`, line220). The independent screenshot review records a readable Replay panel at Tick0 of70 with no explicit error banner; it does not prove the harness predicate passed.

The current response collector at `scripts/acceptance/verify-native-acceptance.mjs:55` includes JavaScript and CSS only. Its requestfailed filter at line71 also excludes art PNG and atlas JSON. It listens to pageerror, not console messages. Empty errors and assetFailures therefore do not rule out either image requests failing or Phaser logging image-processing failures.

Replacement launch runs inside the old Game's DESTROY listener (`src/main.ts:185`). Phaser `node_modules/phaser/src/core/Game.js:733` emits that event before destroying the old renderer at line739, removing the canvas at line748 and destroying its loop at line757. A synchronous replacement exception could abort the remaining teardown because the event emitter invokes listeners directly and runDestroy has no finally. No preceding exception was saved, and each Game owns separate caches and texture managers. This ordering is a conditional failure or resource-pressure hypothesis, not an established explanation for the partial atlases. Independent inspection found no cross-game cache invalidation path; WebGL canvases are not pooled for reuse. A cached-manifest callback being skipped would leave this new ArtRuntime.manifest null and assets zero, which does not match this snapshot.

## Next bounded observation

Preserve the failure and keep the art predicate. The smallest proof-only candidate adds an episode label to replay imports, records console error/warn and webglcontextlost, records status and requestfailed for all `/assets/` URLs, authenticates the actual manifest response, and records each readiness component at timeout: loading overlay hidden, rts present, camera present, canvas present and art.loaded. Keep response observations bounded to the single admitted import episode; do not retain image bodies for every prior replacement. If source-level diagnostics are separately admitted, snapshot the first failed ArtRuntime.ready predicate, its invocation count and required-versus-resident texture keys immediately during create. None of those observations requires changing a game action or weakening readiness.

A fresh-page native import of the interrupted replay is a useful first bounded run. Compare with the moving replay, which has the same initial envelope, if needed. A pass in a fresh page would establish that the isolated input can load; it would not prove why the long sequence failed. Stop before playback if artwork remains incomplete. Extending the wait alone cannot fix a one-time false completeness result.
